Everything below is read from the source.
`tests/unit/test-exports.typ` holds `lib.typ` to a list of public names, so an accidental export cannot slip in, though nothing yet checks that list against this page.

Keisen has no release yet, so import `lib.typ` from a clone rather than from Typst Universe.
A Typst package specification cannot carry a subpath, so once released the integration module under `src/` will not be reachable as `@preview/keisen:0.1.0/src/...`; how those renderers reach an installed package is an open question in the issue list.

## Entry point

```typst
display-table(
  data,                    // first positional: rows or columns
  ..directives,            // any number of directives, applied in order
  theme: theme-default(),  // option dictionary
  spec: none,              // a built specification, rendered instead
)
```

`data` is either an array of dictionaries, one per row, or a dictionary of equal-length arrays, one per column.
Every row gains a reserved `_index` key holding its position in the input, which is what row predicates read.

Directives are plain dictionaries applied in the order written.
For a given cell and property the last matching directive wins, so "format the column, then override a few rows" reads the way it is written.

## Selectors

Three arguments recur throughout, and all three accept the same shapes.

| Argument | Accepts |
| --- | --- |
| `columns` | `auto`, a name, an array of names, or a predicate `name => bool`. |
| `rows` | `auto`, an index, an array of indices, or a predicate `row => bool`. |
| `groups` | `auto`, a label, an array of labels, or a predicate `label => bool`. |

: Selector shapes {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[20,80]"}

Every predicate takes exactly one argument.
Typst closures fail on arity mismatch, and `row => row.margin < 0.05` is what people write, so row position travels on `row._index` rather than as a second parameter.

## Table parts

| Function | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `table-header(title: none, subtitle: none)` | The title block above the column labels. |
| `table-stub(rowname: none, group: none, label: none, indent: none)` | Promotes a column to row names, optionally another to group labels, and a column of integers to indentation levels. |
| `table-spanner(label, columns, level: 1)` | Labels a run of adjacent columns. Higher levels stack above lower ones. |
| `table-source-note(note)` | An unmarked note in the footer. |
| `table-footnote(note, locations: none, mark: auto)` | A marked note. Without locations it is an unmarked footer note. |
| `table-style(properties, locations: none)` | Applies a style to the cells a location names. |
| `table-options(..keys)` | Merges option keys into the theme. |

: Table parts {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[45,55]"}

Row groups render as level-3 native subheaders, so a group spanning a page break reprints its label under the column labels.

## Columns

| Function | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `columns-label(..pairs)` | Named arguments map a column name to its label. Labelling the row-name column labels the stubhead. |
| `columns-align(alignment, columns: auto)` | Sets alignment, direction-relative (`start`, `end`) or absolute. |
| `columns-width(widths)` | A dictionary of column name to length, fraction, or `auto`. |
| `columns-hide(..columns)` | Removes columns from the table; they stay readable by predicates and formatters. |
| `columns-move(..columns, before: none, after: none)` | Reorders columns relative to another column. |

: Column directives {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[45,55]"}

## Formatters

Each takes `columns` as a required first positional argument and `rows` as a named one.
`columns` is required rather than defaulted because a Typst positional parameter cannot carry a default, so "every column" is written explicitly as `auto`.

| Function | Notable arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `format(columns, function, rows: auto)` | Any `value => content`. The escape hatch the others are built on. |
| `format-number(columns, ..)` | `decimals: 2`, `significant: none`, `grouping: 3`, `group-separator`, `decimal-separator: "."`, `scale: 1`, `sign: false`, `rounding: "half-up"`, `negative-zero: false`, `prefix`, `suffix`. |
| `format-integer(columns, ..)` | `format-number` with no fractional part. Passing `decimals` is an error. |
| `format-percent(columns, ..)` | `decimals: 1`, `scale: 100`, `symbol: [%]`, `space: true`. |
| `format-currency(columns, ..)` | `currency: "EUR"`, `decimals: auto`, `symbol: auto`, `position: start`, `space: auto`. |
| `format-scientific(columns, ..)` | `decimals: 2`, `exponent: "power"` or `"e"`. |
| `format-bytes(columns, ..)` | `base: 1024`, `decimals: 1`. |
| `format-date(columns, ..)` | `pattern: "[year]-[month]-[day]"`. Takes a `datetime` or an ISO-8601 string. |
| `format-markup(columns, ..)` | Evaluates a string of Typst markup. No arguments of its own. |
| `format-nanoplot(columns, ..)` | `plot`, `width: 4em`, `height: 0.8em`, `baseline: 15%`, `domain: auto`. |
| `substitute-missing(columns, ..)` | `replacement: [--]`. Applies to `none`, empty strings, and `float.nan`. |
| `substitute-zero(columns, ..)` | `replacement: [--]`. Tests the raw value, before any formatter scales or rounds it. |

: Value formatting {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[35,65]"}

All rounding and scaling happen in Typst's `decimal` type, which is fixed-point, so `0.145` at two decimals is not at the mercy of binary representation.
`rounding: "half-up"` matches `calc.round`; `"half-even"` is implemented in the package for anyone expecting R's behaviour.
Substitutions run before formatting, so a gap never reaches a formatter that would refuse it.

`format-currency` knows EUR, GBP, USD, JPY, and CHF, and writes any other currency as its code, since there are more currencies than anyone should hard-code.
`decimals: auto` follows the currency, so a yen figure carries none.
`symbol: auto` and `space: auto` follow it too: the symbol leads against its number, or trails behind a non-breaking space, as each convention writes it.

`format-scientific` counts the exponent off the digits and cuts the mantissa from them rather than computing either, so it keeps the digits the value had and works on magnitudes `decimal` cannot hold, which is what the notation is for.
Rounding that carries into the next power moves the exponent with it, so nothing renders as `10.0 × 10³`.

`format-bytes` counts in 1024s by default and says so with the binary prefixes; `base: 1000` gives the decimal ones.
Bytes themselves are whole, so the smallest unit carries no fractional part.

`format-date` takes a `datetime` or an ISO-8601 string, since that is how a date arrives from a file: `2026-08-14`, `2026-08-14T09:30:00`, or the space-separated spelling exports write, with or without seconds and with or without a trailing `Z`.
A date that does not exist is refused by pre-check rather than handed to `datetime`, which would panic in a grammar the reader did not write.
`pattern` is Typst's own, so anything `datetime.display` accepts works, and Typst reports a pattern it does not.

`format-date` and `format-markup` both produce opaque content, so neither is decimal-aligned: there is no separator in a date to line up on, and a cell of markup is whatever it evaluates to.

### Nanoplots

A nanoplot cell holds an array of readings, and `format-nanoplot` draws it through the function given as `plot`.
The domain spans every reading in the column, taken from the column itself, so the cells can be compared; that is the whole point, since sparklines scaled per cell say nothing.
`domain: (low, high)` overrides it for a column read against a scale that is not its own.

Three renderers ship, each drawn with native Typst primitives and each usable as `plot`.

| Function | Notable arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `nanoplot-line(numbers, ..)` | `domain: none`, `width: 4em`, `height: 0.8em`, `stroke: auto`, `thickness: 0.6pt`. A sparkline. |
| `nanoplot-points(numbers, ..)` | The same, plus `radius: 1pt`. A sparkline with its readings marked. |
| `nanoplot-bar(numbers, ..)` | `domain: none`, `width: 4em`, `height: 0.8em`, `fill: auto`, `gap: 30%`. Bars, measured from zero. |

: Nanoplot renderers {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[35,65]"}

`stroke: auto` and `fill: auto` follow the surrounding text colour, so a plot in a styled cell is drawn in that cell's ink.
Bars are measured from zero rather than from the domain's low, because a bar drawn from 5 to 10 makes a small difference look like the whole quantity; the line renderers scale to the domain instead, since a trend is about shape rather than magnitude.

A renderer is any `(numbers, domain: none, width: .., height: ..) => content`, so one written in a document works exactly as well as these.

## Locations

`table-style` and `table-footnote` take one location or an array of them.

`cells-body(columns: auto, rows: auto)`, `cells-stub(rows: auto)`, `cells-stubhead()`, `cells-row-groups(groups: auto)`, `cells-column-labels(columns: auto)`, `cells-column-spanners(spanners: auto)`, `cells-title(parts: ("title", "subtitle"))`, `cells-summary(groups: auto, columns: auto, rows: auto)`, `cells-grand-summary(columns: auto, rows: auto)`, `cells-source-notes(notes: auto)`.

A summary row answers to the label that names it and to its position within the group, so `rows: "Subtotal"` and `rows: 0` reach the same row.
`columns: none` is the cell carrying the row's own label, which is how a note goes on the row once rather than on every cell of it.

A location expands against the table into `(part, row, column)` addresses.
This is the part Typst show rules cannot express: they select by element type in document order and never see the row behind a cell.

`style(text: none, fill: none, stroke: none, align: none, inset: none)` builds the properties.
Only what is set appears, so a later style overrides property by property.

`data-colour(palette, columns: auto, rows: auto, domain: auto, target: "fill", missing: none, reverse: false)` maps a column onto a palette.
The domain spans the rows the directive matches, which is every row by default and is what makes per-group scaling a matter of one `data-colour` per group.
With `target: "fill"` the text colour is chosen per cell from its background's relative luminance, so a dark fill never carries unreadable text.

## Aggregations

`summary-rows(functions: (:), columns: auto, groups: auto, format: none)` closes each group; `grand-summary-rows(functions: (:), columns: auto, format: none)` closes the body.
`functions` maps a label to an aggregation, and an aggregation is any `values => value`.

| Function | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| `aggregate-sum`, `aggregate-min`, `aggregate-max` | Stay in decimal arithmetic, so a total is exact. |
| `aggregate-mean`, `aggregate-median` | Convert to float, since division must. |
| `aggregate-count` | Counts values that are present, of any type. |
| `aggregate-standard-deviation` | The sample definition, with `n - 1` in the denominator. |
| `aggregate-quantile(probability)` | Linear interpolation between order statistics, matching R's type 7 default. |

: Built-in aggregations {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[40,60]"}

Aggregations run on raw values before formatting, so a summary cell formats through whichever directive covers its column, or through its own `format:`.

## Themes and options

`theme-default()`, `theme-booktabs()`, `theme-compact()`, and `theme-minimal()` each return an option dictionary, so a preset and a `table-options()` call are the same kind of thing and compose by merging.
Striping is `row-striping: true` on any of them, and the academic three-line style is `theme-booktabs()` plus options; a theme that differs by one boolean is not a theme.

Option names are Typst identifiers, so they are written unquoted: `table-options(row-striping: true)`.
An unknown key is an error rather than a silent no-op, and `tests/unit/test-options-read.typ` holds every declared key to being read by something, so a key that accepts a value and changes nothing cannot ship.

| Group | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| Table | `table-font`, `table-font-size`, `table-align`, `table-border-top`, `table-border-bottom`, `breakable`, `infer-alignment`, `decimal-align` |
| Header | `header-title-size`, `header-title-weight`, `header-subtitle-size`, `header-align`, `header-border-bottom` |
| Column labels | `column-labels-weight`, `column-labels-size`, `column-labels-border-top`, `column-labels-border-bottom`, `spanner-border-bottom` |
| Stub and groups | `stub-weight`, `stub-indent-step`, `row-group-weight`, `row-group-fill`, `row-group-border-top`, `row-group-repeat` |
| Body | `row-striping`, `row-striping-fill`, `cell-inset` |
| Summaries | `summary-weight`, `summary-fill`, `summary-border-top`, `grand-summary-border-top` |
| Footer | `footnote-marks`, `footnote-size`, `source-note-size`, `footer-border-top` |

: Theme options {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[25,75]"}

## Specifications built elsewhere

`display-table(spec: ..)` renders a specification instead of data and directives, which is how a generator in another language reaches this pipeline without emitting table markup.
A specification that arrives as data, from `json()` or from a tool, cannot carry closures, so it names what it wants:

```json
{
  "kind": "display-table",
  "data": [{"product": "Bolt", "region": "North", "units": 1250, "margin": 0.182}],
  "header": {"title": "Regional sales"},
  "stub": {"rowname": "product", "group": "region"},
  "formats": [{"name": "format-integer", "columns": "units"}],
  "summaries": [{"name": "aggregate-sum", "label": "Subtotal", "columns": ["units"]}],
  "styles": [
    {
      "style": {"text": {"weight": "bold"}},
      "part": "body",
      "columns": "margin",
      "rows": {"column": "margin", "op": "<", "value": 0.05}
    }
  ]
}
```

Formatters and aggregations are named from the built-ins, and row predicates are comparisons with `op` in `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `==`, `!=`, composed with `and`, `or`, and `not`.
Comparing against `null` asks whether the cell is empty, which is the only way JSON has to spell absence.
Every key is checked, inside a descriptor as well as at the top level, so a misspelled `columns` fails rather than quietly widening what it applies to.
That is the whole subset: no arithmetic, no function calls, no set tests.
Anything more expressive belongs in a Typst specification, which keeps the schema from drifting into an expression language.

A serialised specification is turned back into ordinary directives and folded through the same path as a hand-written table, so the two cannot diverge: one pipeline, entered two ways.
`examples/serialised.typ` renders `examples/table-spec.json` and compiles with the test suite.

## Limitations

- Summary rows require groups, from `table-stub(group: ..)`; use `grand-summary-rows` for a table without them.
- A combined column is not yet available; `columns-combine` is planned.
- A column of nanoplots cannot be summarised: a series of readings has nothing to aggregate, and saying so is an error rather than a plot of a total.
